text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates. One key part of clean code is following naming conventions. Use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions so others can quickly see what they do. It is also important to keep functions small and focused on a single task. This makes your code easier to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain. When you need to fix a bug or add a new feature later, well-organized code saves you time and reduces mistakes.
